habitat: Pairs or flocks in bushveld and broad-leaved woodland, especially mopane. Flocks come to drink after sunset.
summary: A common near-endemic resident. Usually in pairs. The male has black-and-white bars on the forehead, a white and black band on the breast, and white spots on the back. The female is almost completely speckled. Both sexes have fine black barring on the belly. The call is chuck-chuck, and flocks coming to drink call “Don’t weep so Charlie”. The Kemp paper name Doublebanded Sandgrouse and the code RB were left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common near-endemic resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Eye and bill colours were not described, so they are not stored from the photographs. No flight pattern was described. The grade A call is from Lephalale in Limpopo, not from inside Kruger. A grade A song from Kruger National Park, XC177778, was not selected because the call-typed file ranks first. Population figures and the Kemp name Doublebanded Sandgrouse were left unchanged.
